v: His parents went every year to Jerusalem at the feast of the Passover.
When he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast,
and when they had fulfilled the days, as they were returning, the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem. Joseph and his mother didn’t know it,
but supposing him to be in the company, they went a day’s journey, and they looked for him among their relatives and acquaintances.
When they didn’t find him, they returned to Jerusalem, looking for him.
b: This passage describes Jesus' experience at age twelve, when he went up to Jerusalem with his parents for the Passover. In that era a twelve-year-old boy was already regarded as coming of age, so taking part in such a festival showed that Jesus was moving toward adulthood. On the way home, however, Jesus did not leave Jerusalem with his parents but stayed behind in the temple. His parents did not at first notice he was missing, and only after a day's journey did they realize he was gone, which shows their trust in Jesus and their habit of relying on the large group traveling together.

Jesus' staying in the temple was no accident. It shows his zeal for God's work and a spiritual awareness beyond his years. Although he was still young, he already understood his relationship with the Father and felt a deep concern for his Father's house. This reminds us that spiritual growth and responding to God's call are not limited by age but depend on love for God and the pursuit of him. Jesus' action also challenges us to ask: do we have the same zeal to seek God's house and his will?

When Jesus' parents found he was not with them, they immediately returned to Jerusalem, showing their love for their son and their sense of responsibility. This passage also reminds us that when we find ourselves lost or off course spiritually, we should return at once to God's presence and seek his guidance and light. The parents' anxiety and their search for Jesus is a call to us in our spiritual life: however far we have wandered, God is always waiting for us to return to his arms.
q: When you find yourself lost or astray spiritually, how do you return to God? Do you have, like Jesus, a zeal and longing for God's house?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for letting us see, through Jesus' example, a love for your house and a longing for your will. Help us, wherever and whenever, to stay focused on seeking your heart, and to return to your presence at every moment in our spiritual life. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: After three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the middle of the teachers, both listening to them, and asking them questions.
All who heard him were amazed at his understanding and his answers.
When they saw him, they were astonished, and his mother said to him, “Son, why have you treated us this way? Behold, your father and I were anxiously looking for you.”
He said to them, “Why were you looking for me? Didn’t you know that I must be in my Father’s house?”
They didn’t understand the saying which he spoke to them.
b: In this passage we see the conversation between the young Jesus and the teachers in the temple. He sat among the teachers, listening to them and asking questions, which showed his hunger to learn and his deep understanding of God's law. Everyone present was amazed at Jesus' wisdom and his answers, which reflected the divine wisdom he was born with and foreshadowed his future role as teacher and prophet.

When his parents finally found him, Mary reproached him for causing them anxiety. It was a moment full of human feeling, showing his parents' love and concern for Jesus. Yet Jesus' reply revealed that he knew his mission. His reply, "Didn't you know that I must be in my Father's house?", shows his awareness of his divine mission and a strong sense of calling from childhood, which left his parents puzzled, because they did not yet fully understand his destiny.

This passage reminds us that on our journey of faith we too may sometimes not understand God's works and will. Like Jesus' parents, we may feel confused or perplexed, but that does not mean God's plan is not going forward. Instead, we should learn to trust God. Even though we do not always understand what he is doing, we believe his plan is best, and we keep pursuing a closer relationship with him so that we may understand his will more clearly.
q: When you meet spiritual questions you do not understand, how do you keep trusting God and seeking his will?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us, through Jesus' example, how to seek your will and mission. Give us wisdom and patience, so that when we do not understand your works we can still trust you and work to understand your heart. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: And he went down with them, and came to Nazareth. He was subject to them, and his mother kept all these sayings in her heart.
And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and men.
b: This passage records Jesus' growth through childhood and youth. Although Jesus knew his divine mission well, he still obediently returned to Nazareth and grew up within his family. This shows that his life on earth was fully human. He respected his parents' authority, setting us an example of obedience and respect for parents. Although Jesus was the Son of God, he did not refuse the responsibilities of being human because of that identity, but perfectly fulfilled every duty a child should.

As Jesus grew, "Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and men," which shows his well-rounded growth. He matured in wisdom, deepened in his relationship with God, and won the affection of others in his relationships with people. This is the goal of growth every believer should pursue: balanced development in wisdom, spiritual life and relationships, so that God's work in our lives may be displayed.

This passage reminds us that growth is not only outward physical development; what matters more is growth in wisdom and spirit. We should learn from Jesus' example, seeking growth in wisdom in daily life and working to build deep relationships with God and others. Our growth should be a whole-person process, including spiritual, intellectual and social development, so that we better reflect God's image and will.
q: In your life, how do you pursue balanced growth in wisdom, spirit and relationships? How can you remain faithful to and trust in God at every stage of growth?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for letting us see the example of Jesus' growth. Give us wisdom and strength, so that we may keep growing in spirit, wisdom and relationships. May our whole lives reflect your glory, and may we remain faithful to and trust in you at every stage of growth. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judea, and Herod being tetrarch of Galilee, and his brother Philip tetrarch of the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene,
in the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came to John, the son of Zacharias, in the wilderness.
He came into all the region around the Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance for remission of sins.
As it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet, “The voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make ready the way of the Lord. Make his paths straight.
Every valley will be filled. Every mountain and hill will be brought low. The crooked will become straight, and the rough ways smooth.
All flesh will see God’s salvation.’ ”
b: This passage portrays the calling and mission of John the Baptist in the wilderness. He was called by God to be the forerunner of Jesus Christ and to prepare the way for the Lord. John's message centered on a baptism of repentance, which was not merely a symbolic act but a call to true repentance of the heart. Repentance is the foundation of the Christian life: it means turning to God, leaving behind past wrongdoing, and pursuing a new life.

John's call came in the wilderness, which symbolizes that God's work often begins in the places and moments we least expect. The wilderness is a desolate place, but it is also where God calls and shapes people's lives. This reminds us that, whatever circumstances we are in, as long as we are willing to listen to God's voice, he can open up a new path in our lives.

John quoted the prophecy of Isaiah, showing that his mission was part of God's plan of salvation. The words of that prophecy, "Every valley will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be brought low; the crooked will become straight," symbolize that God is going to change our lives and remove the obstacles so that we can receive his grace. This passage encourages us, as we wait for God's salvation, to prepare our hearts and let him make our paths straight.
q: In your journey of life, are there places that need to be made straight? How can you let God change your life and bring you closer to his salvation?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for reminding us, through the call of John the Baptist, how important repentance is. Help us make straight the paths in our hearts, so that our lives may be ready to welcome your coming. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: He said therefore to the multitudes who went out to be baptized by him, “You offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?

Therefore produce fruits worthy of repentance, and don’t begin to say among yourselves, ‘We have Abraham for our father;’ for I tell you that God is able to raise up children to Abraham from these stones!
Even now the ax also lies at the root of the trees. Every tree therefore that doesn’t produce good fruit is cut down, and thrown into the fire.”
b: In this passage John the Baptist warned the crowds coming to be baptized in stern words. He called them an "offspring of vipers," a harsh rebuke of their insincere repentance. John made clear that true repentance is not an outward form but an inner change, and that this change must bear fruit worthy of repentance.

John's words stress the genuineness of repentance. He warned them not to rely on their ancestors' faith as a guarantee of their own salvation, because God's judgment shows no partiality on account of bloodline. This reminds us that genuine faith does not lie in our background or tradition, but in our real relationship with God and the spiritual fruit our lives bear.

Finally, John used the picture of "the ax is already laid at the root of the trees" to remind us of the urgency of judgment. This means God's judgment may come at any moment, so we must always be ready and bear spiritual fruit as proof of our true repentance and faith. This passage challenges us to examine our lives to see whether we are bearing fruit worthy of repentance, and reminds us that only true repentance and obedience to God's will can stand before his judgment.
q: In your life of faith, are you bearing fruit worthy of repentance? How can you show your true faith in God in daily life?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for reminding us, through John the Baptist's warning, of the genuineness of repentance. Help us bear fruit worthy of repentance, so that our faith is not merely outward form but a real change deep within. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: The multitudes asked him, “What then must we do?”
He answered them, “He who has two coats, let him give to him who has none. He who has food, let him do likewise.”
Tax collectors also came to be baptized, and they said to him, “Teacher, what must we do?”
He said to them, “Collect no more than that which is appointed to you.”
Soldiers also asked him, saying, “What about us? What must we do?” He said to them, “Extort from no one by violence, neither accuse anyone wrongfully. Be content with your wages.”
b: In this passage the crowds reacted strongly to John the Baptist's teaching and asked how they should repent and act. John's answers were not complicated but practical and concrete guidelines for conduct. He stressed the spirit of sharing, telling people to give what they have in excess to those who lack. This is practical care for the poor and needy, and a concrete expression of a changed life after repentance.

To the tax collectors, John said to be honest and not collect more than was due. Tax collectors were then seen as symbols of greed and injustice, so John's teaching was a call to their professional ethics, asking them to change their ways after repenting and to show integrity and fairness of character.

To the soldiers, John stressed not using violence or extorting others, and urged them to be content. This shows that repentance is not only an inner change but should also be reflected in our conduct and attitudes, especially in how we treat others. This passage challenges us to consider whether, after repenting, our way of life and conduct reflect God's justice and love.
q: In your life, how do you turn a repentant heart into practical action? Do you show God's justice and love in your dealings with others?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for reminding us, through John the Baptist's teaching, how to live after repentance. Help us live out your justice and love in daily life, so that our conduct may glorify your name. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: As the people were in expectation, and all men reasoned in their hearts concerning John, whether perhaps he was the Christ,
John answered them all, “I indeed baptize you with water, but he comes who is mightier than I, the strap of whose sandals I am not worthy to loosen. He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire,
whose fan is in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor, and will gather the wheat into his barn; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.”
b: This passage records the people's expectation about John the Baptist and shows how John turned the focus to the coming Christ. The people wondered whether John might be the Christ, which shows their longing and hope for a Savior. John, however, humbly pointed out that the true Christ had not yet come, that he was greater than John, and that John was not even worthy to untie his sandals.

John declared that the coming Christ would baptize not only with water but with the Holy Spirit and fire. This is a powerful prophecy that the coming of Jesus Christ would bring a brand new spiritual baptism, one that is not merely symbolic but the real, life-changing work of the Holy Spirit. The symbol of fire also points to cleansing and judgment, showing that Christ would usher in an age that separates good from evil.

John went on to explain that Christ holds a winnowing fork in his hand to clear his threshing floor, meaning that he will separate those who truly repent and bear fruit from false believers who do not repent. This passage reminds us that Christ's coming will bring real judgment and cleansing, so we need to prepare ourselves before he comes, letting our lives bear the fruit of true repentance to welcome him.
q: In the light of Christ, is your life ready to welcome his coming? How can you bear the fruit of true repentance?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for reminding us, through John the Baptist, of the coming of Jesus Christ and his judgment. Help us prepare our hearts to welcome your Son, and bear the fruit of repentance in our lives. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Then with many other exhortations he preached good news to the people,
but Herod the tetrarch, being reproved by him for Herodias, his brother’s  wife, and for all the evil things which Herod had done,
added this also to them all, that he shut up John in prison.
b: This passage records the courage and outspokenness of John the Baptist. John not only proclaimed the gospel of repentance to the people but also dared to rebuke King Herod, the powerful ruler of the day, because Herod had married Herodias, his brother's wife, a serious sin under the law. John's frankness angered Herod, and in the end he was thrown into prison.

John's courage and his insistence on justice are an example for every believer. He was not afraid of power or of the possible consequences, because he knew that what he preached was God's truth. This passage challenges us to ask whether, like John, we can stand up for the truth under any pressure, whatever the cost. Is our faith firm enough that we can speak out boldly in the face of injustice?

Herod's reaction shows how those in power resist and oppose the truth. This reminds us that when we bear witness to the truth, we may face opposition and persecution from the world. Yet we must not shrink back in fear, because we know that the God we serve is the God of truth, and he will in the end judge all injustice.
q: In your life, have you ever been afraid of the consequences and unwilling to bear witness to the truth? How can you strengthen your faith to speak boldly for God's truth?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for letting us see, through John the Baptist, the courage to bear witness to the truth. Give us the same courage, so that we can stand fearlessly and speak for your truth, whatever the cost. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Now when all the people were baptized, Jesus also had been baptized, and was praying. The sky was opened,
and the Holy Spirit descended in a bodily form like a dove on him; and a voice came out of the sky, saying “You are my beloved Son. In you I am well pleased.”
b: This passage records the baptism of Jesus, a moment of divine significance. Jesus received John's baptism, which was not only a confirmation of identity but also marked the beginning of his public ministry. Although Jesus was sinless, he chose to be baptized to show that he identified with sinners, foreshadowing that he would one day lay down his life for the sins of the world.

When Jesus was baptized, heaven was opened and the Holy Spirit descended on him in the form of a dove, symbolizing the Spirit's anointing and God's confirmation of his mission. This scene reminds us that Jesus' ministry was entirely led and supported by the Holy Spirit, and that all his actions were carried out within God's plan and will. It also challenges us to ask whether our ministry and life are likewise led by the Holy Spirit and accomplished in his strength.

The voice from heaven clearly declared that Jesus is God's beloved Son and that he pleased God. These words not only confirmed Jesus' divine identity but also showed the Father's satisfaction with and support for him. This passage reminds us that, as Christians, our goal should be to please God: whatever we do, we should seek God's will and rely on his strength to accomplish it.
q: In your daily life, do you rely on the Holy Spirit's guidance? How can you make sure your actions and decisions please God?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for showing us, through Jesus' baptism, his divine identity and mission. Help us rely on the guidance of the Holy Spirit, so that everything we do may glorify you and please you. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Jesus himself, when he began to teach, was about thirty years old, being the son (as was supposed) of Joseph, the son of Heli,
the son of Matthat, the son of Levi, the son of Melchi, the son of Jannai, the son of Joseph,
the son of Mattathias, the son of Amos, the son of Nahum, the son of Esli, the son of Naggai,
the son of Maath, the son of Mattathias, the son of Semein, the son of Joseph, the son of Judah,
the son of Joanan, the son of Rhesa, the son of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, the son of Neri,
the son of Melchi, the son of Addi, the son of Cosam, the son of Elmodam, the son of Er,
the son of Jose, the son of Eliezer, the son of Jorim, the son of Matthat, the son of Levi,
the son of Simeon, the son of Judah, the son of Joseph, the son of Jonan, the son of Eliakim,
the son of Melea, the son of Menan, the son of Mattatha, the son of Nathan, the son of David,
the son of Jesse, the son of Obed, the son of Boaz, the son of Salmon, the son of Nahshon,
the son of Amminadab, the son of Aram, the son of Hezron, the son of Perez, the son of Judah,
the son of Jacob, the son of Isaac, the son of Abraham, the son of Terah, the son of Nahor,
the son of Serug, the son of Reu, the son of Peleg, the son of Eber, the son of Shelah,
the son of Cainan, the son of Arphaxad, the son of Shem, the son of Noah, the son of Lamech,
the son of Methuselah, the son of Enoch, the son of Jared, the son of Mahalaleel, the son of Cainan,
the son of Enos, the son of Seth, the son of Adam, the son of God.
b: This passage records the genealogy of Jesus, which is vital for understanding his historical background and divine identity. By recording Jesus' genealogy, Luke connects him with Adam, which not only shows that Jesus is a real historical person but also stresses the universality of his role as Savior of all humanity. Jesus' genealogy includes many great figures of the faith, which reminds us how God's plan of salvation runs through all of history and reaches its climax in Jesus.

This genealogy especially emphasizes Jesus' identity as the "Son of God," a title that shows his divinity and his central place in the plan of redemption. As a descendant of Adam, Jesus bore the sins of all humanity and, through his sacrifice, brought us salvation. This reminds us that Jesus came not only for the nation of Israel but for all humankind, and his work of redemption unites all believers and makes us children of God.

This passage also prompts us to reflect on our place in God's plan of salvation. Every believer is part of God's family line, because through Jesus Christ we have become children of God. We should be thankful for and treasure this identity, and strive to live a life worthy of it, becoming witnesses of God's kingdom and showing his love and grace.
q: In your life of faith, how do you live out your identity as a child of God? How can you better bear witness to God's salvation and love?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for making us your children and letting us take part in your plan of redemption through Jesus Christ. Help us treasure this identity and live a life worthy of it, to the glory of your name. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan, and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness
for forty days, being tempted by the devil. He ate nothing in those days. Afterward, when they were completed, he was hungry.
The devil said to him, “If you are the Son of God, command this stone to become bread.”
Jesus answered him, saying, “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.’ ”
b: This passage records Jesus facing the devil's temptation in the wilderness. Having just been baptized and filled with the Holy Spirit, he was led into the wilderness, where he went through forty days of fasting and testing. Here we see that before Jesus began his public ministry, he first faced a spiritual trial. It reminds us that as Christians we too will face temptation and testing, and that these trials often come at the very moment of spiritual renewal or when we are preparing for a new calling.

The devil first attacked Jesus' physical need, challenging him to turn stones into bread. This was not only about hunger; it was also a challenge to his identity: "If you are the Son of God." Yet Jesus did not give in. He answered the devil with Scripture, stressing that true life depends on the word of God and not on material satisfaction. This answer upholds the priority of the spiritual over the physical, and it sets an example for us: when we are tempted, we should rely on God's word rather than yield to the demands of the moment.

This passage teaches us that spiritual strength comes from depending on God's word, not from worldly satisfaction. When we face temptation or challenge, we can remember Jesus' example and stand firm on God's word. God's word is our shield in temptation, protecting us from the devil's attacks.
q: Are you facing temptation in your life right now? How can you rely more fully on God's word to meet these challenges?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us your word so that we can stand firm in temptation. Help us to rely on your word in every challenge, and let the example of Jesus guide us to live a life that pleases you. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: The devil, leading him up on a high mountain, showed him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.
The devil said to him, “I will give you all this authority, and their glory, for it has been delivered to me; and I give it to whomever I want.
If you therefore will worship before me, it will all be yours.”
Jesus answered him, “Get behind me Satan! For it is written, ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and you shall serve him only.’ ”
b: In this passage the devil tempts Jesus further, this time trying to lure him into yielding with earthly authority and glory. The devil claims to hold power over the world and offers to give it all to Jesus if only he will bow down before him. This temptation strikes at the human desire for power and splendor, yet once again Jesus firmly refuses with the word of God, declaring that worshiping and serving God alone is the only right choice.

Jesus' reply tells us that true authority and glory come from God, not from worldly power. This passage reminds us that when temptation comes, however attractive it may look, we must stay faithful to God, and remember that real satisfaction and honor come from serving God, not from surrendering to worldly allurements. Jesus sets an example here: in the face of temptation, hold fast to faith and worship God alone.

This passage teaches us that when worldly power and splendor tempt us, we need to examine the motives of our hearts. Have we neglected the worship of God and our faithfulness to him in pursuit of worldly success? We should learn from Jesus' example and, in every circumstance, worship God alone without being swayed by the temptations of the world.
q: In pursuing worldly success, have you neglected your faithfulness to God? How can you keep your worship of God undivided in daily life?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for showing us how Jesus remained faithful to you in temptation. Help us, when we face worldly allurements, to hold fast to our faith as Jesus did, to worship you alone, and to make your glory the goal of our lives. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: He led him to Jerusalem, and set him on the pinnacle of the temple, and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, cast yourself down from here,
for it is written, ‘He will put his angels in charge of you, to guard you;’
and, ‘On their hands they will bear you up, lest perhaps you dash your foot against a stone.’ ”
Jesus answering, said to him, “It has been said, ‘You shall not tempt the Lord your God.’ ”
b: In this passage the devil tempts Jesus a third time. He takes Jesus to the pinnacle of the temple and challenges him to prove that he is the Son of God. The devil quotes Scripture, trying to persuade Jesus to throw himself down, since God would surely send angels to protect him from harm. This temptation challenges faith and trust in God, but Jesus answers without hesitation, quoting Scripture, firmly refusing the devil's challenge and telling him, "You shall not test the Lord your God."

Jesus' answer stresses that trust in God should be unconditional, not something that demands proof of God's love and protection by putting him to the test. This passage reminds us to depend on God with simple, trusting hearts, rather than demanding that God prove his love or protection for us in some special way. We should trust God's plan and his will for us, and not question or challenge his work by testing him.

This passage teaches us that when we face the uncertainties and challenges of life, we should trust God's wisdom and his plan, rather than trying to prove God's love through testing or challenge. We should follow Jesus' example, keeping our trust in God in every situation and not letting outside pressure shake our faith.
q: When you face uncertainty in life, have you ever doubted God's love and protection? How can you trust his plan better in those moments?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us, through the example of Jesus, how to trust your will and your plan. Help us, when we face uncertainty and challenge, to rely on you rather than to test or question your love and protection. May our faith keep growing and standing firm under your guidance. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: When the devil had completed every temptation, he departed from him until another time.
Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit into Galilee, and news about him spread through all the surrounding area.
He taught in their synagogues, being glorified by all.
b: This passage describes the scene after Jesus overcame the temptation. When the devil had exhausted every kind of temptation, he left Jesus for a time. Then Jesus, in the power of the Spirit, returned to Galilee and began his public ministry. This passage reminds us that even though Jesus faced severe temptation, he kept his complete trust in God, and so he was filled with the Spirit's power, and his fame spread quickly because of his teaching and his deeds.

Everyone praised Jesus' teaching, which shows that his words carried great authority and attraction. This passage reminds us that when we overcome temptation by the Spirit's power, God gives us even greater power to accomplish his work. Jesus' example encourages us: whatever challenge we face, as long as we keep relying on the Spirit, our ministry too can be blessed by God and become a blessing to others.

This passage teaches us that the Christian life should be founded on the power of the Holy Spirit, depending on God in every challenge and temptation. When we do this, our lives become a testimony to God's mighty power, and our influence will spread among the people of the world, bringing glory to God's name.
q: When you face temptation or challenge in life, how do you rely on the Spirit's power to overcome? Is your life bearing witness to God's power to those around you?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us the power of your Holy Spirit so that we can stand firm in temptation. Help us rely on the Spirit's guidance, so that always and everywhere we live out your will and spread your love and truth. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: He came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up. He entered, as was his custom, into the synagogue on the Sabbath day, and stood up to read.
The book of the prophet Isaiah was handed to him. He opened the book, and found the place where it was written,

“The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent me to heal the broken hearted, to proclaim release to the captives, recovering of sight to the blind, to deliver those who are crushed,
and to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord.”
b: This passage describes Jesus beginning his public teaching in the synagogue at Nazareth. On the Sabbath, as was his custom, Jesus went into the synagogue and stood up to read a passage from the prophet Isaiah. This passage foretells the mission of the Messiah and stresses the work he would do: proclaim good news to the poor, announce release to the captives, give sight to the blind, and set the oppressed free. By this Jesus declared his mission and ministry, showing that he came into the world to fulfill these promises.

Jesus' announcement at Nazareth marked the beginning of his ministry and showed that he fully identified with the prophet's words: he is the one anointed by God to carry out God's plan of redemption. This passage reminds us that Jesus' mission is to bring liberation, healing, and freedom, which is the heart of the gospel message. As his followers, we too are called to take part in this mission and to pass this good news on to those around us.

This passage teaches us that Jesus' mission is not only spiritual salvation; it is also to bring real change and liberation into our daily lives. We should think about how we can put Jesus' teaching into practice, helping the oppressed and the poor, and showing God's love and justice at every level of life.
q: How do you put Jesus' teaching into practice in your life, to help those who are oppressed and in need? How could you share the good news of the gospel more effectively?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us Jesus Christ, who came into the world to bring us the good news of the gospel. Help us to live out Jesus' mission in our daily lives, to be his witnesses, and to carry the good news of liberation and healing to everyone. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: He closed the book, gave it back to the attendant, and sat down. The eyes of all in the synagogue were fastened on him.
He began to tell them, “Today, this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
All testified about him, and wondered at the gracious words which proceeded out of his mouth, and they said, “Isn’t this Joseph’s son?”
b: This passage records how Jesus responded after reading from Scripture in the synagogue at Nazareth. When he had finished reading the prophecy of Isaiah, he rolled up the scroll and told the people, "Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing." These words plainly declared that Jesus is the Messiah who fulfills the prophet's words. The people were amazed at his words and spoke well of him, but they were also puzzled, because they thought he was only the son of Joseph the carpenter, whom they knew so well.

Jesus' declaration shows that God's promise has been fulfilled in his coming. This was a challenge not only to the people in the synagogue at that time, but also to every one of us. Do we believe that Jesus is the Savior sent by God? Is the gospel he brings being truly fulfilled in our lives? Jesus' words remind us that the power of the gospel is real and can be truly experienced in our lives.

This passage teaches us that Jesus is the one God sent to fulfill his promises. We should receive his words in faith and bear witness in our lives to the fulfillment of those promises. Let us not allow familiarity to cloud our recognition of who Jesus truly is, but receive the salvation he brings with humble hearts.
q: In your life, have Jesus' teachings and promises been fulfilled? How can you experience more deeply, and bear witness to, what he is doing in your life?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for sending Jesus Christ among us to fulfill your promises. Help us to receive his words in faith and to bear witness in our lives to his truth and power. May our lives reflect his glory. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: He said to them, “Doubtless you will tell me this parable, ‘Physician, heal yourself! Whatever we have heard done at Capernaum, do also here in your hometown.’ ”
He said, “Most certainly I tell you, no prophet is acceptable in his hometown.
But truly I tell you, there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the sky was shut up three years and six months, when a great famine came over all the land.
Elijah was sent to none of them, except to Zarephath, in the land of Sidon, to a woman who was a widow.
There were many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, yet not one of them was cleansed, except Naaman, the Syrian.”
b: In this passage Jesus foresees the people's doubt and rejection of him, and quotes the proverb "Physician, heal yourself" to describe the difficulty he would meet in his hometown. Jesus points out that a prophet is often not accepted in his own country, a pattern seen again and again in history. He goes on to give examples: the prophets Elijah and Elisha were rejected in Israel, yet their ministries were received among the Gentiles.

These words of Jesus were a challenge to his townspeople, who thought they knew him. They considered themselves familiar with Jesus, yet could not see his true identity and mission. His words remind us not to overlook what God is doing in someone simply because we are familiar with that person. We should receive God's work with an open heart, whatever channel or person it comes through.

This passage teaches us that when familiarity keeps us from accepting what God is doing, we need to adjust our attitude and outlook. We should recognize that God's work and plans often go beyond our understanding, so we should receive his guidance with humility and not reject his truth because of our prejudices or fixed ideas.
q: In your life, have there been times when familiarity led you to overlook or reject what God was doing? How can you keep a humble and open heart to receive his guidance?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us through Jesus a humble and open attitude. Help us, when we face what is familiar, not to overlook your work because of prejudice. May our hearts always stay humble and willing to receive your guidance and teaching. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: They were all filled with wrath in the synagogue, as they heard these things.
They rose up, threw him out of the city, and led him to the brow of the hill that their city was built on, that they might throw him off the cliff.
But he, passing through the middle of them, went his way.
b: This passage describes the anger that Jesus' sermon stirred up in the synagogue at Nazareth. When he explained that he was the Messiah sent by God and revealed the history of Israel's rejection of the prophets, the people in the synagogue could not accept the rebuke. Their anger reached such a pitch that they wanted to throw Jesus off the cliff. Yet by his divine power Jesus passed straight through the midst of them and was not harmed.

This passage reflects the resistance and hostility people may show when God's truth touches the depths of their hearts. Here Jesus shows his commitment to the truth: even facing the threat of death, he did not shrink back. His actions teach us that when we face opposition and hostility, we too should hold to the truth and trust God's protection and guidance.

This passage teaches us that as Christians, when we stand up to bear witness to the truth, we may sometimes face opposition and hostility from others. Yet Jesus' example tells us to press on without fear, trusting that God will be with us, protect us, and give us the victory.
q: When you meet opposition because you hold to your faith, how do you stand firm in the truth and rely on God's protection? Are you ready to face such challenges?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us Jesus as our example, teaching us how to hold to the truth in the face of hostility. Give us courage and strength so that we can keep holding to your word in hard times and face every challenge in faith. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: He came down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee. He was teaching them on the Sabbath day,
and they were astonished at his teaching, for his word was with authority.
b: This passage describes Jesus' teaching in Capernaum and how the people reacted to his words. Jesus came down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and taught the people on the Sabbath. His teaching was full of authority. Unlike the religious leaders of the day, his words carried an incomparable power, and the people were amazed and astonished at his teaching.

Jesus' teaching was full of authority because he is the Son of God, and his words carry God's truth and power. This passage reminds us that as followers of Jesus, we too should make his words the foundation of our lives and trust in their power and authority. Jesus' teaching is not merely the passing on of knowledge; it is truth with the power to change lives.

This passage teaches us that we should listen to Jesus' teaching and obey it with reverence and faith. His words are full of God's authority, able to guide us along the right path and make a deep impact on our lives. We should strive to apply these teachings in our daily lives and make them the cornerstone of our faith.
q: Do you sincerely listen to Jesus' teaching and obey it? How do these teachings make a difference in your life?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us Jesus Christ, so that through his teaching we can understand your will. Help us to listen to and obey his words with faith and reverence, and to make them the foundation of our lives. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: In the synagogue there was a man who had a spirit of an unclean demon, and he cried out with a loud voice,
saying, “Ah! what have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are: the Holy One of God!”
Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be silent, and come out of him!”  When the demon had thrown him down in the middle of them, he came out of him, having done him no harm.
Amazement came on all, and they spoke together, one with another, saying, “What is this word? For with authority and power he commands the unclean spirits, and they come out!”
News about him went out into every place of the surrounding region.
b: This passage records Jesus casting out an unclean spirit in the synagogue, a moment that displayed his divine authority. When a man possessed by an unclean spirit cried out defiantly in the synagogue, Jesus rebuked the spirit without fear and commanded it to come out of the man. The miracle amazed the people, because they saw the authority and power in Jesus' words.

This event made people realize that Jesus' words were not only teaching; they had power to change reality, even to cast out unclean spirits. The people were astonished and began to recognize Jesus' divine identity and the mission for which he came into the world. This passage reminds us that Jesus' authority is above all evil powers, and that in every difficulty and challenge of our lives he can bring salvation and freedom.

This passage teaches us that when we face spiritual attack or difficulty, we should rely on Jesus' authority and power. He has already overcome evil, and in him we can find protection and comfort. We should stay alert at all times and trust in the name of Jesus, because his authority is enough for every challenge in our lives.
q: When you face spiritual challenges or difficulties, do you rely on Jesus' authority? How can you keep your faith and trust in those moments?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us Jesus Christ, whose authority and power overcome all evil. Help us, when we face spiritual attack, to find protection and freedom in the name of Jesus, and to walk in your will in faith. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: He rose up from the synagogue, and entered into Simon’s house. Simon’s mother-in-law was afflicted with a great fever, and they begged him for her.
He stood over her, and rebuked the fever; and it left her. Immediately she rose up and served them.
b: This passage describes the miracle of Jesus healing Simon's mother-in-law after he entered Simon's house. Simon's mother-in-law was bedridden with a severe illness, but when Jesus stood over her and rebuked the fever, it left her at once, and she was immediately restored to health and got up to serve Jesus and the others. This miracle once again shows Jesus' power to heal and his authority over sickness.

Jesus' healing was not only to free people from the pain of illness, but to restore their health so that they could return to ordinary life and ministry. As soon as Simon's mother-in-law was healed, she got up and served, which shows that God's healing has a purpose: not merely our personal comfort, but that we might serve him better.

This passage teaches us that when we call on Jesus, he has the power to heal our body, mind, and spirit, so that we may be restored and continue working for him. Whatever illness or difficulty we face, we should come to Jesus in faith and trust his great power and compassion. God's healing is not only the removal of pain; it is so that we may live a full life and pass on his love and grace to others.
q: After you have experienced God's healing or help, how do you respond to his grace with action? In what ways could you serve God and others better?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for the healing that comes through Jesus Christ, which lets us recover from illness. Help us, once we are restored, to give our lives wholly to you and to respond to your love with action, serving you and others. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: When the sun was setting, all those who had any sick with various diseases brought them to him; and he laid his hands on every one of them, and healed them.
Demons also came out of many, crying out, and saying, “You are the Christ, the Son of God!” Rebuking them, he didn’t allow them to speak, because they knew that he was the Christ.
b: This passage describes Jesus healing a great crowd of sick and demon-possessed people at sundown. The people brought all their sick to Jesus, and whatever the illness, Jesus laid his hands on each one and healed them by his grace and power. This scene reveals Jesus' unconditional love and his deep concern for human suffering. Jesus not only healed bodily diseases but also cast out demons, restoring people in body and mind.

Jesus rebuked the demons that came out of people and would not allow them to speak publicly about who he was. This shows Jesus' control over his mission and his unwillingness to have evil spirits reveal his identity. He wanted people to come to know him through faith and his teaching, not through the voice of evil spirits. It also reminds us that true faith comes from the heart's acceptance and trust, not from outward voices or proclamations.

This passage teaches us that Jesus is our healer and savior. Whatever difficulty or illness we meet, if we are willing to come to him in faith, he can heal us and set us free. Jesus' love and power are limitless, and his salvation is not only for our bodies but is complete, embracing our hearts and souls.
q: When you face illness or difficulty, are you willing to bring it to Jesus, trusting that his great power and love can bring healing and release?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us Jesus Christ, who heals our body, mind, and spirit so that we may be made whole. Help us to look to Jesus in hardship and to trust his salvation and his healing power. May our lives be filled with your peace and grace. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: When it was day, he departed and went into an uninhabited place, and the multitudes looked for him, and came to him, and held on to him, so that he wouldn’t go away from them.
But he said to them, “I must preach the good news of God’s Kingdom to the other cities also. For this reason I have been sent.”
He was preaching in the synagogues of Galilee.
b: This passage describes Jesus leaving the crowds one morning to go to a solitary place and pray. The people were unwilling to let him go and wanted him to stay with them. Yet Jesus knew his mission and purpose clearly, and told them that he must keep preaching the good news of the kingdom of God in other towns, because that was why he was sent. This shows Jesus' firm commitment to his mission and that he was not bound by any place or person.

Jesus' reply tells us that he came into the world to save the world, and that his message and salvation are not confined to one place but are prepared for all people. This passage reminds us that the gospel is universal: wherever we are and whoever we are, we all need to hear and receive this message of salvation.

This passage teaches us that as followers of Jesus we too are called to proclaim the gospel of the kingdom of God. We cannot stay in one comfortable place; we must carry the fire of the gospel to more people and proclaim the salvation of Jesus Christ. We should learn from Jesus' example, steadfastly fulfilling God's calling and taking the gospel to the ends of the earth.
q: In your life, are you willing to share the gospel with more people? How can you respond more actively to God's call in daily life and become a messenger of his gospel?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us Jesus Christ, who showed us how to faithfully complete your mission. Help us to proclaim the gospel boldly in our lives, unlimited by circumstances, and to submit willingly to your sending, bringing your love to more people. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: Now while the multitude pressed on him and heard the word of God, he was standing by the lake of Gennesaret.
He saw two boats standing by the lake, but the fishermen had gone out of them, and were washing their nets.
He entered into one of the boats, which was Simon’s, and asked him to put out a little from the land. He sat down and taught the multitudes from the boat.
b: This passage describes Jesus teaching beside the Lake of Gennesaret. The people, eager to hear the word of God, pressed in around Jesus, so that he had to get into a boat to teach. Jesus chose Simon's boat and asked him to put out a little from the shore so that he could teach the crowd better. This scene shows Jesus' care for the people and how he used the resources at hand to carry out his work of teaching.

Jesus' choice to step into Simon's boat was no accident; it would become the beginning of a larger plan. Jesus' teaching was not only the giving of knowledge but carried the power to call and to change. Everything he did had deep meaning, showing his complete submission to God's will and his plan to bring about the kingdom of God.

This passage teaches us that when Jesus enters our lives, he brings not only the teaching of truth but also an invitation to take part in his work. Our daily life, our work, and our resources can all become tools God uses to carry out his plan. Like Simon, we should be willing to offer what we have to the Lord and let him use it to bless more people.
q: In your life, how do you let Jesus use your resources to bless others? Are you willing, like Simon, to place your resources at Jesus' disposal?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for teaching us the truth through Jesus Christ and for inviting us to take part in your work. Help us to be willing to offer our lives, our work, and our resources to you, so that they may become tools you use to spread the gospel and bless others. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, “Put out into the deep, and let down your nets for a catch.”
Simon answered him, “Master, we worked all night, and took nothing; but at your word I will let down the net.”
When they had done this, they caught a great multitude of fish, and their net was breaking.
They beckoned to their partners in the other boat, that they should come and help them. They came, and filled both boats, so that they began to sink.
b: In this passage we see Jesus give Simon a command that seems simple but is in fact full of challenge: put out into the deep water and let down the nets for a catch. Simon had just spent a tiring and fruitless night, and his professional knowledge and experience as a fisherman left him doubtful, yet out of trust in Jesus he chose to obey. When Simon did as Jesus said, he experienced a supernatural miracle and caught a larger quantity of fish than ever before.

This miracle shows Jesus' sovereignty and control over nature, and it also shows us that when we obey Jesus' word, his blessing often goes beyond our expectations and understanding. Simon's obedience brought an astonishing result, and it reminds us that whatever difficulty or challenge we meet in life, trusting and obeying Jesus' word is the key to blessing and breakthrough.

This passage teaches us that whatever our experience or circumstances, when Jesus speaks we need to trust him wholeheartedly. Jesus' words carry power, and he can bring abundant fruit out of situations that seem hopeless. Like Simon, we should lay aside our doubts and act on Jesus' guidance, and then we will experience his abundant blessing.
q: In your life, have you relied on your own experience and overlooked Jesus' guidance? How can you trust and obey his word more fully in specific situations?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us Jesus Christ, whose words are full of power and wisdom. Help us, in every challenge and difficulty, to rely wholeheartedly on Jesus' guidance, to obey his word, and to trust that he will bring abundant blessing. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: But Simon Peter, when he saw it, fell down at Jesus’ knees, saying, “Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, Lord.”
For he was amazed, and all who were with him, at the catch of fish which they had caught;
and so also were James and John, sons of Zebedee, who were partners with Simon. Jesus said to Simon, “Don’t be afraid. From now on you will be catching people alive.”
When they had brought their boats to land, they left everything, and followed him.
b: This passage records Simon Peter's reaction after seeing Jesus' miracle. He felt deeply unworthy and recognized his own sinfulness, so he fell down at Jesus' knees and asked Jesus to go away from him. Yet Jesus did not withdraw because of Peter's self-awareness; instead he gave him a brand-new mission: to become a fisher of men. This call changed the lives of Peter and the other disciples, and they left everything at once and followed Jesus.

Peter's reaction shows us that when we truly experience Jesus' power and holiness, we too come to see our own shortcomings and sinfulness. This awareness is not meant to drive us away from Jesus; it should make us come to him more humbly and receive his grace and his call. Jesus did not reject Peter because of his weakness; he gave him a new identity and mission.

This passage teaches us that Jesus' call is powerful. He sees not only our faults but also our potential and the mission he wants to give us. When we hear Jesus' call, we should be willing, like Peter, to leave everything and follow him. It is a brand-new beginning, and he will lead us on a path unlike any before, a path full of purpose and grace.
q: What is Jesus' call in your life? Are you willing to set aside your personal pursuits and follow him wholeheartedly, to become a worker in his kingdom?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us Jesus Christ, whose call has given us new birth out of sin. Help us to respond boldly to Jesus' call, to be willing to leave everything and follow him, and to become workers in his kingdom. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: While he was in one of the cities, behold, there was a man full of leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he fell on his face, and begged him, saying, “Lord, if you want to, you can make me clean.”
He stretched out his hand, and touched him, saying, “I want to. Be made clean.” Immediately the leprosy left him.
He commanded him to tell no one, “But go your way, and show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing according to what Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.”
But the report concerning him spread much more, and great multitudes came together to hear, and to be healed by him of their infirmities.
But he withdrew himself into the desert, and prayed.
b: In this passage we see a man covered with leprosy come to Jesus and beg him to make him clean. The man knew his condition well, and his request was full of faith and humility. Jesus did not turn him away; instead, with love and compassion, he reached out and touched him and declared him clean. That one touch not only healed his body but also restored his dignity, bringing him back from the margins of social exclusion into the community.

Jesus told the man to do what the law required and show himself to the priest as a testimony of his cleansing. This was a sign that his cleansing was not only spiritual but also met the requirements of the law. Jesus' action shows his care for both the individual and society. He not only heals people spiritually but also respects the justice of the law and the order of society.

This passage teaches us that Jesus' healing and salvation are complete. He sees our needs and is willing to reach out his hand to help us. When we come to him in faith, his compassion and power bring change to us. We should also learn from Jesus' example and, under his leadership, become messengers of love and compassion, caring for those who are overlooked or excluded by society.
q: Around you, are there people who are overlooked or excluded? How are you willing to follow Jesus' example and bring them love and compassion?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us Jesus Christ, whose love and compassion help us stand again in hard times. Help us follow Jesus' example, be a blessing to others, and pass on your love in our society. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: On one of those days, he was teaching; and there were Pharisees and teachers of the law sitting by, who had come out of every village of Galilee, Judea, and Jerusalem. The power of the Lord was with him to heal them.
Behold, men brought a paralyzed man on a cot, and they sought to bring him in to lay before Jesus.
Not finding a way to bring him in because of the multitude, they went up to the housetop, and let him down through the tiles with his cot into the middle before Jesus.
Seeing their faith, he said to him, “Man, your sins are forgiven you.”
b: This passage records an extraordinary event that took place while Jesus was teaching. A group of men brought their paralyzed friend to Jesus, but because of the crowd they could not get near him. They decided to go up on the roof, remove the tiles, and lower their friend down on his mat right in front of Jesus. When Jesus saw their strong faith, he immediately declared that the paralytic's sins were forgiven.

This story highlights the power of faith. The men's actions showed their firm trust in Jesus' great power: they were willing not only to overcome obstacles but also to act boldly to seek healing for their friend. Jesus saw their faith and responded to it, healing not only the paralytic's body but, more importantly, forgiving his sins, so that he was completely healed spiritually as well.

This passage teaches us that faith is the key to God's grace. When we come to Jesus with sincere faith, he not only answers our needs but also gives deeper spiritual blessings. Jesus values our faith; he is willing to heal our bodies and willing to forgive our sins, making us whole in spirit. Like these friends, we should bring the needs of others to Jesus and become a blessing in their lives.
q: In your life, are you willing to come to Jesus in faith and to intercede for others, so that they too may experience God's grace and healing?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us Jesus Christ, whose love and power have changed our lives. Strengthen our faith, so that we may come to Jesus in faith and intercede for others, that they too may experience your healing and forgiveness. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: The scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, “Who is this that speaks blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone?”
But Jesus, perceiving their thoughts, answered them, “Why are you reasoning so in your hearts?
Which is easier to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven you;’ or to say, ‘Arise and walk?’
But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins” (he said to the paralyzed man), “I tell you, arise, take up your cot, and go to your house.”
Immediately he rose up before them, and took up that which he was laying on, and departed to his house, glorifying God.
Amazement took hold on all, and they glorified God. They were filled with fear, saying, “We have seen strange things today.”
b: This passage describes how Jesus, after forgiving the paralytic's sins, faced the questioning of the Pharisees and the scribes. These religious leaders believed that only God can forgive sins, and so they considered Jesus' words blasphemy. Yet Jesus knew their thoughts and asked a challenging question: which is easier, to say "Your sins are forgiven" or to say "Rise up and walk"? By this Jesus showed that he has authority on earth to forgive sins, and he performed a miracle, so that the paralytic was healed at once and went home carrying his mat.

This miracle shows not only Jesus' power over disease but also his authority to forgive sins. Jesus' action proved his divinity to the people: he can heal not only the sicknesses of the body but also the wounds of the soul. The miracle amazed the people, and they gave glory to God, because they had seen the wonders God did through Jesus.

This passage teaches us that Jesus is the Lord who has authority to forgive sins and to heal, and that we should trust him wholeheartedly and bring to him both bodily sickness and spiritual struggles. Jesus' grace is limitless: he is willing to heal our wounds and forgive our sins so that our lives may be renewed. Let us learn from those who witnessed the miracle and give glory to God, because he has done wonderful things in our lives.
q: In your life, do you fully trust Jesus' power to forgive and heal? How can you bring your difficulties to him and let him heal and renew your life?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us Jesus Christ, who has authority to forgive sins and to heal. Help us to rely on him wholeheartedly in hard times, to trust his great power and grace, and to entrust our lives completely to you. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: After these things he went out, and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax office, and said to him, “Follow me!”
He left everything, and rose up and followed him.
Levi made a great feast for him in his house. There was a great crowd of tax collectors and others who were reclining with them.
Their scribes and the Pharisees murmured against his disciples, saying, “Why do you eat and drink with the tax collectors and sinners?”
Jesus answered them, “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick do.
I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
b: This passage records the process of Jesus calling Levi (Matthew) to follow him. As a tax collector, Levi was regarded by Jewish society at that time as unclean and a sinner. Yet Jesus took the initiative and came to his workplace and gave him a simple but powerful call: "Follow me!" Levi left everything without hesitation and followed Jesus, an act that showed his faith in Jesus and his determination.

Levi's following not only changed his own life but also influenced those around him. Levi held a great banquet for Jesus at his house and invited many other tax collectors and sinners. This drew criticism from the Pharisees and the scribes, who were displeased that Jesus associated with such "unclean" people. Jesus answered them, pointing out the purpose for which he came: not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance. His words reveal his mission: he came into this world to save those who admit that they need salvation.

This passage teaches us that Jesus' call makes no distinction between high and low. He is willing to save everyone, whatever our past, and as long as we are willing to repent and follow him, he can change our lives. Jesus' mission is to call sinners to repentance, which is an enormous grace to us. We should be thankful for Jesus' mercy and respond to his call, following him without reservation, as Levi did.
q: In your life, is there any obstacle that keeps you from following Jesus fully? How can you overcome these obstacles and respond to his call?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank you for giving us Jesus Christ, who calls us to repentance and to follow him. Help us, like Levi, to respond to Jesus' call without reservation and to entrust our lives completely to you. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: Thank you, Holy Spirit, for leading us to understand the truth and to live it out. May God bless you.

v: They said to him, “Why do John’s disciples often fast and pray, likewise also the disciples of the Pharisees, but yours eat and drink?”
He said to them, “Can you make the friends of the bridegroom fast while the bridegroom is with them?
But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them. Then they will fast in those days.”
He also told a parable to them. “No one puts a piece from a new garment on an old garment, or else he will tear the new, and also the piece from the new will not match the old.
No one puts new wine into old wine skins, or else the new wine will burst the skins, and it will be spilled, and the skins will be destroyed.

q: 在您的生活中，您是否有機會以超越世俗的方式去愛那些不配得愛的人？您如何能夠展現神的慈悲心？

The good man out of the good treasure of his heart brings out that which is good, and the evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart brings out that which is evil, for out of the abundance of the heart, his mouth speaks.

q: 在您的生命中，您是否注重內心的建造，並讓基督的愛和真理充滿您的心靈？如何能夠在日常生活中結出屬靈的好果子？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您藉著耶穌基督教導我們內在生命的重要性。求您幫助我們時常省察自己的內心，並讓我們的心靈被您的愛和真理所充滿。願我們的言行能夠結出美好的果子，成為他人的祝福，並榮耀您的名。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: “Why do you call me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ and don’t do the things which I say?
Everyone who comes to me, and hears my words, and does them, I will show you who he is like.

He is like a man building a house, who dug and went deep, and laid a foundation on the rock. When a flood arose, the stream broke against that house, and could not shake it, because it was founded on the rock.
But he who hears, and doesn’t do, is like a man who built a house on the earth without a foundation, against which the stream broke, and immediately it fell, and the ruin of that house was great.”
b: 這段經文中，耶穌提出了一個對信仰生活極其重要的問題：為什麼稱祂為「主」，卻不照祂的話去行？這是一個深刻的反思，提醒我們信仰不僅僅是口頭上的認同或形式上的敬拜，更需要在生活中實踐出來。耶穌強調，真正的信仰應該建立在祂的話語之上，並且通過具體的行動來表現。
耶穌以蓋房子的比喻來說明這個道理。那些聽見祂的話並且遵行的人，像是將房子建在堅固的磐石上。這樣的房子在面對風暴時依然穩固，不會倒塌。這比喻告訴我們，當我們將信仰的根基深植在耶穌的教導上，無論遇到什麼樣的試煉或挑戰，我們的生命都能經受住考驗。
另一方面，那些聽見但不遵行的人，就像是在沙土上建房子。這樣的房子雖然在外表上看起來與前者相似，但缺乏穩固的基礎，在風暴來臨時必然會倒塌。這提醒我們，若我們的信仰只是表面功夫，沒有真正將耶穌的話語融入生活中，那麼當困難來臨時，我們的生命也將無法承受。

for he loves our nation, and he built our synagogue for us.”

b: 這段經文記載了耶穌治癒一位百夫長的僕人的故事，這位百夫長的信心在福音書中被高度讚揚。百夫長是一位外邦人，但他對耶穌有著極深的信任和敬畏，甚至認為自己不配見耶穌，只求耶穌一句話就能醫治他的僕人。這樣的信心和謙卑使得耶穌對他颳目相看，並藉此教導眾人。
百夫長的信心不僅僅是一種抽象的信念，而是基於他對權柄的理解。他明白自己作為一個有權柄的人，可以發號施令，同樣地，他也相信耶穌擁有超自然的權柄，可以只靠一句話就使他的僕人得醫治。這種對耶穌權柄的信任，成為了福音書中信心的典範。
耶穌對百夫長的讚賞告訴我們，真正的信心不是來自於我們的身份或背景，而是來自於我們對耶穌的完全信任和順服。這提醒我們，在我們的生活中，也要學習百夫長的信心和謙卑，相信耶穌的權能，相信祂的每一句話都帶有能力，能夠改變我們的處境。
q: 在面對困難時，您是否像百夫長一樣，全心信靠耶穌的權柄？如何在您的信仰生活中更深地依靠祂的話語？
真理傳遞 第 135 課 想的威力
「想」 是很重要的過程。牠讓我們的意念變成可能。許多的研究和計畫，都是從一個意念，經過反復的想和嘗試而漸漸邁向成功的\!意念就像種子，雖然小卻能長成一棵大樹。人類歷史上的偉大發現和發明都是上帝賜給人靈感和從上帝來的意念，當人相信並反復思想成爲觀念而且付諸行動就能成就上帝的心意和工作。
上帝渴望我們參與祂的計畫，上帝將祂的心意放在我們心裡 ，祂要我們藉著我們的「求」和「想」來參與祂的工作。 「成就」是上帝的工作，我們的責任 就是「求」和「想」。

當我們「求」和「想」，上帝就能夠成就。好像一個婦人祈求要孩子。當她懷孕時就已經「得著」。她不需要再祈求了，可是還沒有「成就」\! 她需要經過孕育的過程，直到產期到了，孩子生下來，就是「成就」了\! 就像哈拿沒有孩子在聖殿不斷的傾心吐意的祈求，上帝藉著祭司以利說，願耶和華應允你所求的，哈拿相信了祭司的話語，她領受了，就起來吃飯不再憂傷，因為他心裡已經得著上帝的應許，她回去跟丈夫同房，上帝就讓她懷孕，直到孩子生下來，長大之後來到聖殿去還願，就是因為她已經得到也拿到應許，而應許也成就了，所以她就歸榮耀與上帝，獻祭給上帝。
我們有需要的時候就會產生祈求。而上帝說話就會回應我們的祈求，當上帝答應我們祈求的，就是得著了應許。我們就不必再祈求，而是要開始想，在心中想，去孕育上帝所應許話語的胎兒，所以我們要開始操練，從「求」到「成就 中間這個「想」的過程。
我們要開始憑著信心靠著聖靈，想象上帝的應許成為我們心中的藍圖，成為信心的實底和確據。就能夠帶出信心的行動去應用直到成就，就應驗了應許。所以應許是得到，應用是做到，應驗是拿到。這過程我們要去操練，但前提是我們要先求到上帝說話，上帝對我們應許，然後你才藉著應許來思想，不是我們自己憑空的想，按著自己的思慾來妄求，而是有實底有確據的想。
從「得著」到「成就」，是需要經過一段時間。我們若懷疑或放棄，就如同「流產」或「墮胎」，上帝的應許就不能成就了 。上帝應許的成就需要時間，需要過程，需要信心，需要孕育，需要培養，更需要忍耐。所以我們要存心忍耐，耐心等候。等候耶和華的必然得福。
「想」是一個很有威力的工具。正確的「想」可以讓我們經歷上帝的作為。我們要謹慎我們所「想」的，不要讓撒但 有機可乘。我們要善用我們的「想」，大膽為主來夢想\!
上帝創造的 靈界法則和自然界的法則，牠有共通點，就是靈界和自然界交流的管道。這是神透過靈界 在自然界 做事的法則，所以我們要明白：
上帝應許的話

上帝會先說話應許我們，因為上帝的話沒有一句不帶著能力的。當上帝說話的時候，我們就要開始思想，思想上帝的話，然後就會產生信心，當我們思想明白了，上帝的話就會產生有生命力的信心在我的裡面，是活潑的信心，這個活潑的信心就會開始在我們的心中產生夢想，這夢想是一種心裡的看見，他看見上帝所成就應許的藍圖，就變成了我們信心的實底和確據，之後我們人就開始用信心的話語，去把神的話說出來，當我們用信心說出上帝的話，上帝的話就會發出能力，也帶出權柄，在自然界成就上帝所要成就的事，就應驗了上帝的工，所以這四原則 是很重要的，就是思想的原則、信心的原則、夢想的原則及言語的原則。透過思想、信心、夢想和言語 使我們可以跟上帝交流，思想成為我們的意念，信心成為我們的實底，夢想成為我們的異象，言語成為我們的宣告，當我們用信心如此行的時侯，就會應驗上帝所應許的話。
魔鬼會彷冒偽裝用欺騙的話，他的思想就是憂慮懼怕的意念，他給我們的信心就是消極負面的信心，他帶給人的惡夢就是黑暗灰色的畫面，他帶給人的言語就是埋怨咒詛的言語。
而上帝訓練亞伯拉罕的信心，也是透過這些原則，因為亞伯拉罕稱為信心之父，他的信心是由小而大，慢慢培養起來的，上帝訓練他的信心， 第一個改他的名字將他改名字叫亞伯拉罕就是多國之父的意思，把他的妻子撒萊 改為撒拉就是多國之母的意思。讓他們每天叫彼此的名字就是宣告是多國之父、多國之母。他們透過聽，去想，當他們成為多國之父、多國之母會是怎樣的情景，他們就開始去思想 上帝的應許。
上帝帶他觀看天上的星，海邊的沙。
應許他說將來你的子孫要如同天上的星和海邊的沙那麼多。所以每次亞伯拉罕看見天上的星星，看到海邊的沙，他就透過看去想，想上帝的應許，想上帝應驗的時候，他的子孫就像天上的星星那麼多。每一顆星就好像代表他一個子孫，每一粒沙也好像代表他的後裔，他這個想就有個實底和確據。他不住的藉著想去孕育他的信心，直到一百歲的時候，他的信心就應驗了，真的生出應許之子以撒。
所以上帝就藉著亞伯拉罕的信心成就上帝的應許。這是我們的信心之父亞伯拉罕被上帝訓練的原則，我相信同樣法則，也是上帝可以訓練我們的，我們要透過聽去想，也透過看去想，而藉著想去孕育信心，藉著信心成就上帝的應許，阿們。
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您藉著百夫長的故事教導我們何謂真正的信心。求您幫助我們像他一樣，以謙卑的心來信靠耶穌，並相信祂的每一句話都有改變生命的能力。願我們在生活中依靠您的話語，見證您的大能。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: Soon afterwards, he went to a city called Nain. Many of his disciples, along with a great multitude, went with him.
Now when he came near to the gate of the city, behold, one who was dead was carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow. Many people of the city were with her.
When the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said to her, “Don’t cry.”
He came near and touched the coffin, and the bearers stood still. He said, “Young man, I tell you, arise!”
He who was dead sat up, and began to speak. And he gave him to his mother.
Fear took hold of all, and they glorified God, saying, “A great prophet has arisen among us!” and, “God has visited his people!”
This report went out concerning him in the whole of Judea, and in all the surrounding region.
b: 這段經文記載了耶穌在拿因城施行一個復活的神蹟，祂讓一個寡婦的獨生子從死裡復活。這是耶穌憐憫心腸的真實表現，祂看到寡婦的痛苦，主動去幫助她，甚至在她還未開口求助之前。耶穌的行動顯示了祂對人類痛苦的深切關懷。
耶穌命令少年人復活的時刻，表現出祂對生命和死亡的絕對權柄。祂不是僅僅來安慰這位悲痛的母親，而是直接介入，改變了她的處境，恢復了她的家庭。這神蹟讓周圍的人驚嘆不已，他們意識到神通過耶穌的行動在他們中間工作，這使他們將榮耀歸於神。
這段經文提醒我們，耶穌不僅僅是一位教導者，祂也是我們的救主，能夠將我們從最深的絕望中拯救出來。無論我們的困境有多麼黑暗，耶穌都能夠帶來希望和生命。祂的憐憫和大能無處不在，祂願意介入我們的生活，為我們帶來轉變。
q: 當您面對生命中的困境時，是否相信耶穌能夠帶來轉變？如何在困難中依靠祂的力量和憐憫？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您賜下耶穌，祂不僅是我們的救主，更是我們在困境中的幫助。求您幫助我們在痛苦和絕望中，依靠耶穌的憐憫和大能，知道祂能夠改變一切。願我們的信心在您的愛中得以堅固，並見證您的大能。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: The disciples of John told him about all these things.
John, calling to himself two of his disciples, sent them to Jesus, saying, “Are you the one who is coming, or should we look for another?”
When the men had come to him, they said, “John the Baptizer has sent us to you, saying, ‘Are you he who comes, or should we look for another?’ ”
In that hour he cured many of diseases and plagues and evil spirits; and to many who were blind he gave sight.

Jesus answered them, “Go and tell John the things which you have seen and heard: that the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have good news preached to them.
Blessed is he who finds no occasion for stumbling in me.”
b: 這段經文描述了施洗約翰在獄中因信仰的試煉而陷入困惑，他派遣門徒去問耶穌是否就是那位要來的彌賽亞。這是一個充滿人性的一刻，即使是像施洗約翰這樣偉大的信仰者，也會在逆境中產生懷疑和困惑。
耶穌並沒有直接回答這個問題，而是列舉了祂所行的神蹟來證明祂就是那位應許的彌賽亞。祂治好了病人，讓瞎子看見，讓死人復活，並向窮人傳福音，這些行動顯示了彌賽亞的職責和使命。耶穌的回應旨在鼓勵約翰堅持信心，認識到神的國已經藉著祂的行動來到。
耶穌最後的一句話，「凡不因我跌倒的，就有福了！」提醒我們，當面臨困難或困惑時，要堅守信仰，不要因環境的挑戰而失去對基督的信心。我們被召來以信心接受耶穌所做的一切，即使在我們不完全明白的時候。
q: 在面對信仰挑戰時，您如何保持對耶穌的信心？當困惑和疑問來臨時，您是否願意回到耶穌的教導和作為中尋求答案？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您通過耶穌向我們顯明祢的真理和愛。求您在我們面臨懷疑和困難時，堅固我們的信心，使我們不因環境而跌倒，能夠堅持相信耶穌是那位應許的救主。願我們在祢的愛中得著平安和力量。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: When John’s messengers had departed, he began to tell the multitudes about John, “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
But what did you go out to see? A man clothed in soft clothing? Behold, those who are gorgeously dressed, and live delicately, are in kings’ courts.
But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and much more than a prophet.
This is he of whom it is written, ‘Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you.’
“For I tell you, among those who are born of women there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptizer, yet he who is least in God’s Kingdom is greater than he.”
When all the people and the tax collectors heard this, they declared God to be just, having been baptized with John’s baptism.
But the Pharisees and the lawyers rejected the counsel of God, not being baptized by him themselves.
b: 在這段經文中，耶穌讚揚了施洗約翰的偉大，並將他與其他先知作對比。約翰不是一個軟弱的人，也不是一個追求奢華生活的人，他是上帝的使者，受命為彌賽亞預備道路。耶穌指出，約翰比所有的先知更偉大，因為他直接為彌賽亞的來臨做了準備。
然而，耶穌也提到，在神的國度裡，最小的比約翰還大。這並不是貶低約翰，而是強調神的國度的獨特性和優越性。當我們進入神的國度，我們的身份和價值超越了地上的一切，無論在世上我們的地位如何，在神國中，我們都被尊榮和重視。
經文還提到，眾百姓和稅吏因為受過約翰的洗禮，願意以神為義，而法利賽人和律法師卻因拒絕接受約翰的洗禮，錯失了神的旨意。這提醒我們，接受神的呼召，順服祂的旨意，是我們進入神國的關鍵。
q: 在您的生活中，您是否願意順服神的旨意，並接受祂的呼召？您如何確保自己在神的國度中尋找到真正的身份和價值？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您通過施洗約翰為我們預備了迎接耶穌的道路。求您幫助我們在生活中謙卑順服，接受祢的呼召，進入祢的國度。願我們在祢的國中找到真正的身份和價值，並以信心行在祢的旨意中。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: “To what then should I compare the people of this generation? What are they like?
They are like children who sit in the marketplace, and call to one another, saying, ‘We piped to you, and you didn’t dance. We mourned, and you didn’t weep.’
For John the Baptizer came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, ‘He has a demon.’
The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you say, ‘Behold, a gluttonous man, and a drunkard; a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’
Wisdom is justified by all her children.”
b: 這段經文記載了耶穌對當時世代的批評，祂指出這個世代的人像是無理取鬧的孩童，無論遇到什麼情況，都不願意作出正確的回應。他們批評施洗約翰過於嚴苛，認為他是被鬼附著的，卻又批評耶穌與罪人交往，稱祂為貪食好酒的人。無論是約翰的禁食生活，還是耶穌的接納和憐憫，都無法滿足這些人的要求。
耶穌指出，這世代的人拒絕了神的使者，無論他們是嚴肅的或是慈愛的，都被誤解和排斥。這種拒絕和頑梗顯示了人心的封閉，他們拒絕接受神的恩典，因為這恩典不符合他們的期望和標準。
然而，耶穌也提醒我們，真正有智慧的人會認識到神的智慧和作為。智慧之子以智慧為是，他們不會被世俗的偏見所蒙蔽，而是看見神在不同的使者和方式中所展現的真理和愛。我們被呼召成為這樣的智慧之子，超越世俗的眼光，接納神所賜的一切。
q: 當您面對社會和環境的壓力時，您是否能超越世俗的偏見，接納神的作為和恩典？您如何在生活中保持智慧，持守真理？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您藉著耶穌和施洗約翰向我們展示了不同的屬靈道路。求您賜給我們智慧，使我們不被世俗的偏見所蒙蔽，而是能夠看見您的作為，並接受您的恩典。願我們在生活中持守真理，成為智慧之子，見證您的榮耀。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。

v: One of the Pharisees invited him to eat with him. He entered into the Pharisee’s house, and sat at the table.
Behold, a woman in the city who was a sinner, when she knew that he was reclining in the Pharisee’s house, brought an alabaster jar of ointment.
Standing behind at his feet weeping, she began to wet his feet with her tears, and she wiped them with the hair of her head, kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment.
Now when the Pharisee who had invited him saw it, he said to himself, “This man, if he were a prophet, would have perceived who and what kind of woman this is who touches him, that she is a sinner.”
Jesus answered him, “Simon, I have something to tell you.” He said, “Teacher, say on.”
“A certain lender had two debtors. The one owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
When they couldn’t pay, he forgave them both. Which of them therefore will love him most?”
Simon answered, “He, I suppose, to whom he forgave the most.” He said to him, “You have judged correctly.”

Turning to the woman, he said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? I entered into your house, and you gave me no water for my feet, but she has wet my feet with her tears, and wiped them with the hair of her head.
You gave me no kiss, but she, since the time I came in, has not ceased to kiss my feet.
You didn’t anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with ointment.
Therefore I tell you, her sins, which are many, are forgiven, for she loved much. But one to whom little is forgiven, loves little.”
He said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”
Those who sat at the table with him began to say to themselves, “Who is this who even forgives sins?”
He said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”
b: 這段經文記錄了耶穌在法利賽人西門家裡的事件，一個罪人女人用香膏和眼淚洗淨了耶穌的腳。這是一個充滿情感和救贖意義的場景，耶穌藉此機會教導了關於愛與赦免的深刻道理。
這個女人的行為顯示了她對耶穌的深深敬愛，她用眼淚和香膏洗耶穌的腳，表達了她的悔改和感激之情。而西門，作為一位法利賽人，雖然邀請耶穌進入他的家，卻未能真正明白耶穌的身份和使命。耶穌藉著一個比喻，指出赦免多的人對祂的愛也更多，這女人因為知道自己罪重，但卻因著耶穌的恩典得赦免，愛耶穌的心也更加深厚。
這段經文提醒我們，耶穌來到世上，正是為了尋找並拯救那些迷失的人。祂不在意我們過去的罪，而是在意我們是否願意悔改並愛祂。當我們深刻體會到耶穌的赦罪恩典時，我們的愛和感激也會不斷增加，這種愛將成為我們生活中的力量和動力。
q: 您是否因為深知耶穌的赦罪恩典，而更深地愛祂？如何在生活中將這份愛化為具體的行動來榮耀祂？
pr: 親愛的天父，感謝您賜下耶穌，祂的愛和赦免是我們最大的寶藏。求您幫助我們深刻體會這份恩典，並以全心全意的愛來回應耶穌的愛。願我們的生命因您的赦免而得著更新，並成為見證您恩典的器皿。奉主耶穌基督的名禱告，阿們。
dc: 感謝聖靈引導我們明白真理，並且遵行真理，願上帝祝福你。
